svg.text: An infographic portrait of the Land of the Rising Sun
Japan is an East Asian archipelago of more than 14,000
islands, stretching from the chilly seas of Hokkaido to the
subtropical reefs of Okinawa. Home to about 124 million
people, it ranks among the world's four largest economies
and is a global leader in technology, automotive
From the neon-lit streets of Tokyo to the serene temples
of Kyoto, the country blends densely urban metropolises
with pristine natural landscapes — a contrast that has
shaped its art, cuisine, and design sensibility for
Japan is a constitutional monarchy whose Emperor serves as ceremonial head of state while the elected Diet governs day to day.
Organised into 47 prefectures across four main islands — Honshu, Hokkaido, Kyushu, and Shikoku — the nation sits on the
Pacific Ring of Fire, making it famously prone to earthquakes and volcanic activity. Despite a rapidly ageing population,
Japan remains one of the world's largest economies by nominal GDP, renowned for its bullet trains, world-class cuisine,
and UNESCO-listed cultural heritage that ranges from ancient temples to the art of sushi-making.
